summary: Oak Island Light, Caswell Beach, NC: a concrete tower lit 15 May 1958 at the Cape Fear entrance, replacing Bald Head's Cape Fear light; climbs run by volunteers.

notes_for_editor: Thin on people: no keeper of the 1958 light is named in any source read; the USLHS place record has a People heading with no names, and the station's roster is empty. The 1849-1894 range lights on Oak Island are a separate record (us-nc-oak-island-range); their keepers (e.g. John G. Brickman, 1851 inspection, per LighthouseFriends) belong there, not here. Heights conflict: LighthouseFriends 158 ft tower; NC Tripping 153 ft; USLHS 169 ft above MHW and 155 ft to lantern centre; the record's focal height (51.5 m) follows USLHS. Range: the record's 22.0 nm is not supported by any source read (LighthouseFriends says visible 24 miles; Wikipedia's nominal 20.5 nm is a lead only). Characteristic Fl(4) W 10s in the record is not confirmed by a readable source; the LED beacon is described only as 'revolving'. Climbing schedule conflicts: the 2026 news report says Thursday and Sunday top tours through Labor Day; NC Tripping (Aug 2026) says Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday May to September and Wednesday and Saturday October to April. Check with the Friends. Friends of Oak Island Lighthouse website (oakislandlighthouse.org) could not be read: the server returns a compressed body that fetch_text does not decode, so its cached copy is binary and unusable for quote checks. The Caswell Beach town page returns 403. The 2002 fire is sourced to Beaufort-NC.com (a travel directory); the Wilmington Star-News report (starnewsonline.com) returned 403. The NRHP nomination PDF (npgallery 07000293) is a 'not yet digitized' placeholder, so no nomination text was used. The 1958 lighting: LighthouseFriends says the keeper climbed a ship's-ladder stair of 134 steps; the 2026 news report and NC Tripping give 131 steps. The story now gives 131 steps (news report, NC Tripping) and 134 (LighthouseFriends), and states the schedule change from 1 October. Chapter choice: the only post-1958 incident in the sources read is the February 2002 fire at the adjoining Coast Guard station (lighthouse undamaged). It is placed under 'After the keepers' because it is not a storm, wreck or rescue at this tower, which keeps the story to the four chapters a moderate-length story allows. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: Added the 2026 news report's change to Wednesday and Saturday top tours from 1 October, and LighthouseFriends' 134-step count against the 131 steps in the news report and NC Tripping. The NRHP asset record's 'Date Published' (4/5/2007) is now given as the record's date rather than as the listing date; a human should confirm the listing date from the NRHP weekly list if it is needed. The 1849 range-light scan pages (20, 155) were confirmed with corpus.py page. The 1958 switch-on and the 169-ft figure come from LighthouseFriends and USLHS; the brief's 22.0 nm range and Fl(4) W 10s characteristic remain unconfirmed by any readable source and are not in the story.
